title: Kato divisorial recognition on saturated complete monoid local models (literature interface)
statement:
Let $P$ be a finitely generated integral saturated commutative monoid [def-trf-fs-log-blowup], written additively, and suppose it is sharp, meaning that $0$ is its only invertible element. Let $n\geq0$ be an integer. For a coefficient ring $L$, write $L[P][t_1,\ldots,t_n]$ for the ring of finite sums of symbols $c z^q t^e$, with $q\in P$, $e\in\mathbf N^n$, $c\in L$, and multiplication $z^qz^{q'}=z^{q+q'}$. If $L$ is local with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m_L$, let $B_L(P,n)$ be its completion [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion] at $(\mathfrak m_L,z^q\ (q\neq0),t_1,\ldots,t_n)$. Let $R$ be one of the following rings: (i) $B_k(P,n)$ for a field $k$; (ii) $B_C(P,n)/(\theta)$ for a Cohen ring $C$ of residue characteristic $p$ [def-weil-pbc-cohen-ring] and $\theta-p\in(z^q\ (q\neq0),t_1,\ldots,t_n)B_C(P,n)$. In case (ii), $p$ is prime and the residue field of $C$ is arbitrary of characteristic $p$. Write $z^q\in R$ for the image of the indicated monomial.  Let $S=\{z^a:a\in P\}\subset R$ be the multiplicative set of all chart monomials, and let $\ell:R\to S^{-1}R$ be the localization homomorphism. Here $S^{-1}R$ consists of fractions $f/s$, with $(f,s)\sim(g,t)$ if $h(tf-sg)=0$ for some $h\in S$. The complete-local divisorial recognition equality is
$$\ell^{-1}\bigl((S^{-1}R)^\times\bigr)=\{u z^a:u\in R^\times,\ a\in P\}.$$
In other words, a regular function on this complete model is invertible after all chart monomials are inverted if and only if it is a chart monomial times a unit of $R$.

source.place: Exposé VI 1.4, printed p. 69 (recognition equality, citing Nizioł 2006, Proposition 2.6), and VI 1.6(i)--(ii), printed p. 70 (complete models). Complete-local recognition interface to Kato 1994, Theorem 11.6 / Nizioł 2006, Proposition 2.6: both primary references WANTED, not read locally.

proof.text: The normality theorem [lem-trf-log-regular-saturation-normality] applies to exactly the two coefficient alternatives in the statement, so $R$ is a nonzero normal domain. Apply the facet-valuation theorem [lem-trf-complete-toric-facet-valuations] to obtain Noetherianity, nonvanishing of all $z^q$, the finite facet set $\mathcal F$, its primitive forms $\nu_F$, the half-space description of $\sigma$, and the boundary primes $\mathfrak p_F$ with $v_F(z^q)=\nu_F(q)$. The saturated-cone theorem [lem-trf-sharp-cone-lattice-intersection] gives that $G=P^{\rm gp}$ is free of finite rank and $P=\sigma\cap G$. All these statements include $P=\{0\}$ and $n=0$.

source.place: Direct algebraic proof for the complete models of ILO VI 1.6, printed p. 70; not an application of VI 1.4.

proof.text: For completeness the normality required by divisor theory is available at every prime. If $x\in\operatorname{Frac}(R)$ is integral over $R_{\mathfrak q}$, choose $s\notin\mathfrak q$ divisible by the finitely many denominators of a monic equation for $x$. The rescaled equation for $sx$ is monic over $R$, so $sx\in R$ and $x\in R_{\mathfrak q}$. Thus all prime localizations are normal domains. They are Noetherian: an ideal of a localization is generated by the images of generators of its contracted ideal, since its denominators are units. For height-one $\mathfrak q$ the local dimension is one, and [lem-sc-normal-dim1-dvr] makes $R_{\mathfrak q}$ a discrete valuation ring. Use its normalized additive valuation $v_{\mathfrak q}$: a nonzero element is a unit times an integer power of a uniformizer, and its value is this exponent [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring]. Values add on products; membership in $R_{\mathfrak q}$ is equivalent to a nonnegative value, and membership in its unit group to value zero.

source.place: Tag 00PD (lemma-characterize-dvr); localization of integral closedness and ideal generators are written out.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sc-divisor-finite-support] to $X=\operatorname{Spec}R$, with its single affine cover: $R$ is a Noetherian domain, so $X$ is integral, its generic local ring is $K=\operatorname{Frac}(R)$, and codimension-one points are height-one primes. The orders in that node agree with the valuations of step 2: in a DVR, for a nonzero element $c=u\pi^e$, the successive quotients of $R_{\mathfrak q}/(c)$ have $e$ residue-field factors, so its length is $e$. Subtracting for a fraction gives $v_{\mathfrak q}$. Consequently every $b\in K^\times$ has a finite principal divisor $\operatorname{div}_R(b)=\sum v_{\mathfrak q}(b)[\mathfrak q]$. Valuation additivity gives $\operatorname{div}_R(bc)=\operatorname{div}_R(b)+\operatorname{div}_R(c)$. Define $\operatorname{Cl}(R)$ as the free abelian group on height-one primes modulo these principal divisors, as in the boundary-injection node.

source.place: Tags 02RL (lemma-divisor-locally-finite), 0BE3 (definition-principal-divisor), 02RP (lemma-div-additive), 0BE4 (definition-class-group); the invoked finiteness theorem is the existing cited node.

proof.text: Take $f\in R$ with $\ell(f)$ a unit. Represent its inverse by $g/z^a$, with $g\in R$, $a\in P$. The equality $\ell(fg)=\ell(z^a)$ gives $z^b(fg-z^a)=0$ for some $b\in P$. By step 1 the monomial $z^b$ is nonzero and $R$ is a domain, so $fg=z^a\neq0$, in particular $f\neq0$. At any height-one prime not among the $\mathfrak p_F$, no monomial lies in the prime by [lem-trf-complete-toric-facet-valuations]; thus $z^a$ is a unit there, and $fg=z^a$ makes $f$ a unit there too. Hence $v_{\mathfrak q}(f)=0$ outside the facet primes. At a facet prime $f$ belongs to its local ring, so $m_F=v_F(f)\geq0$. Therefore $\operatorname{div}_R(f)=\sum_Fm_F[\mathfrak p_F]$.

source.place: Direct algebraic proof for the complete models of ILO VI 1.6, printed p. 70; not an application of VI 1.4.

proof.text: The divisor just obtained is principal, so its class in $\operatorname{Cl}(R)$ is zero. All hypotheses of [lem-trf-complete-toric-boundary-class-injectivity] have been established: the complete model and its coefficient condition are unchanged; step 1 gives the Noetherian normal domain, nonzero monomials, facet ideals, primitive forms, valuation formula, and the exhaustive list of height-one primes meeting the monomials. The class $[(m_F)_F]$ is in the kernel of its injective map $\beta$, so it is zero in $\mathbf Z^{\mathcal F}/\nu(G)$. Thus there exists $g_0\in G$ with $\nu_F(g_0)=m_F$ for every facet $F$. This uses the full integer cokernel; nonnegative principal boundary divisors have not been assumed to be monomials.

source.place: Direct algebraic proof for the complete models of ILO VI 1.6, printed p. 70; not an application of VI 1.4.

proof.text: Since every $m_F\geq0$, the facet half-space description in [lem-trf-complete-toric-facet-valuations] implies $g_0\otimes1\in\sigma$. The equality $P=\sigma\cap G$ in [lem-trf-sharp-cone-lattice-intersection] then gives $g_0=a_0$ for some $a_0\in P$. Saturation is used precisely here; nonnegative facet coordinates alone would not suffice for a non-saturated monoid.

source.place: Direct algebraic proof for the complete models of ILO VI 1.6, printed p. 70; not an application of VI 1.4.

proof.text: The monomial $z^{a_0}$ has valuation $\nu_F(a_0)=m_F$ at each facet prime by [lem-trf-complete-toric-facet-valuations]. At every other height-one prime it is a unit, because that prime contains no monomial. Thus $w=f/z^{a_0}\in K^\times$ has value zero at every height-one prime. Both $w$ and $w^{-1}$ therefore belong to every height-one localization of $R$, by step 2.

source.place: Direct algebraic proof for the complete models of ILO VI 1.6, printed p. 70; not an application of VI 1.4.

proof.text: Step 2 shows that $R$ is a normal ring in the sense that all prime localizations are normal domains. Since it is Noetherian, [lem-weil-pbc-serre-criterion-normal] gives $(S_2)$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-serre-s2-total-fraction-membership] separately to $w$ and $w^{-1}$: $R$ is reduced because it is a domain, its total fraction ring is $K$, and their membership in height-one localizations was proved in step 7. At the only height-zero prime $(0)$ both already belong to $K=R_{(0)}$. Membership in each localization means exactly that some denominator $s\notin\mathfrak q$ clears the fraction to an element of $R$, as that node requires. Hence $w,w^{-1}\in R$. Their product is one in $K$, and $R\hookrightarrow K$ is injective, so $w\in R^\times$ and $f=wz^{a_0}$. This proves the required inclusion by ring arguments alone, with no etale sheaf or descent assertion.

source.place: Tags 031S (lemma-criterion-normal) and 031T (lemma-normal-domain-intersection-localizations-height-1); the cited S2-membership node states the more general codimension-one membership tool.

proof.text: Conversely, if $f=uz^a$ with $u\in R^\times$ and $a\in P$, then $\ell(u)$ is a unit and $\ell(z^a)$ has the inverse $1/z^a$ by the definition of localization. Hence $\ell(f)$ is a unit. This proves equality. If $P=\{0\}$ the facet vector in steps 5--6 is the empty vector and $G=0$, so $a_0=0$ and the conclusion is $f\in R^\times$; also $S=\{1\}$ directly. If $n=0$ there are no parameter variables anywhere in the argument.

source.place: Direct algebraic proof for the complete models of ILO VI 1.6, printed p. 70; not an application of VI 1.4.

proof_origin.place: Direct normal-domain divisor proof for the models in VI 1.6 (printed p. 70), via facet valuations, boundary class-group injectivity, and saturation. VI 1.4 is the motivating recognition statement, not a theorem applied in this proof. The two toric algebra inputs are new unsplit nodes, with Kato/Niziol references WANTED.

tool_uses.why: General one-dimensional normal local algebra identifies the height-one localizations with DVRs; the log unit has no different replacement.

General normal Noetherian rings satisfy S2, needed only for the existing fraction-membership tool.
General codimension-one membership tool applied to w and its inverse; the log unit does not replace this commutative-algebra theorem.

lean.statement: theorem complete_toric_kato_recognition (P : Type u) [AddCommMonoid P] (hP : IsFineSaturatedMonoid (Multiplicative P)) (hsharp : ∀ q : P, IsAddUnit q → q = 0) (n : ℕ) : (∀ (k : Type v) [Field k], (algebraMap (CompletedLocalModel k P n) (Localization (Submonoid.map (completeToricChart k P n) ⊤))) ⁻¹' {x | IsUnit x} = {x | ∃ a : CompletedLocalModel k P n, IsUnit a ∧ ∃ q : Multiplicative P, x = a * completeToricChart k P n q}) ∧ (∀ (C : Type v) [CommRing C] [IsLocalRing C] (p : ℕ), IsCohenRing p C → ∀ θ : CompletedLocalModel C P n, θ - (p : CompletedLocalModel C P n) ∈ completedLocalModelBoundaryIdeal C P n → (algebraMap (cohenCompleteToricRing C P n θ) (Localization (Submonoid.map (cohenCompleteToricChart C P n θ) ⊤))) ⁻¹' {x | IsUnit x} = {x | ∃ a : cohenCompleteToricRing C P n θ, IsUnit a ∧ ∃ q : Multiplicative P, x = a * cohenCompleteToricChart C P n θ q})
lean.note: Uses the published AddMonoidAlgebra.CompletedLocalModel and completedLocalModelBoundaryIdeal from the normality proof dependency; the field and Cohen cases are separate conjuncts and the fs predicate is on Multiplicative P.
